facts.authoredFrom: Read from the case's input bytes: repo/grund.toml alone (version 1, `strict = false`, default kinds, `[scan] include` and extensions). The default `[scan] include` is `["requirements.md", "docs", "e2e", "src"]` from the config root (§FS-config.3.5), and none of it exists, so a run given no path and the editor's run at the root read no file: the catalog is empty. `check` then earns the empty-scan caution's repo-root message (§FS-check.2.2, §FS-check.2.2.2.1) beside the version caution (§FS-check.checks.config-version-1), both site-less CLI-level lines (§FS-check.2.1.1) in the report's bytewise (path, line, message) order (§FS-errors.4.1, §FS-check.checks.config-version-1.1), the version caution first; the base is the config root, so each names `grund.toml` (§FS-cli.3.4). `cover --lines 1` asks of grund.toml, a file of a type grund does not scan, so it produces no record and exits 0 (§FS-cover.6.3). `fmt` over a scope that reads nothing has an empty change set (§FS-fmt.1). FS-404 is the absent control.

path-argument.authoredFrom: The path argument is grund.toml, the one file below the input root. A path argument is read though it lies outside `include` (§FS-scan.path.check), but grund.toml's extension is not among the default extensions (§FS-config.3.5), so the walk reads nothing: the empty-scan caution names that path and the recognized extensions (§FS-check.2.2.2.2), the path spelled from the report base, the config root, as `grund.toml` (§FS-cli.3.4). The version caution sorts first (§FS-errors.4.1). `cover --lines 1` of grund.toml gives no record (§FS-cover.6.3) and `fmt` changes nothing (§FS-fmt.1).

editor-overlay.authoredFrom: The tree has no editable source, so the held edit is a buffer-only agreement-overlay.md at the root, and its saved control is that file on disk (§FS-scan.text.buffer-only). The walk reads or skips it by §FS-scan.scope exactly as the saved file, and the root is under no default `include` entry (§FS-config.3.5), so it is skipped: every tree answer is the whole tree's. `cover --lines 1` is asked of that file, and `--lines` reads the one file it is given (§FS-cover.6.1), a Markdown file whose extension is listed: line 1, `Agreement buffer control.`, is owned by no declaration, so its one record has no owner run (§FS-cover.6.3).
